chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: What is the basis of Satan's authority over humans according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s clarification that Satan’s *slutān* (authority) is not an inherent dominion but a conditional power granted based on human voluntary submission (*ittiba'*). This hadith underscores the Shia theological principle of free will (*ikhtiyar*), distinguishing between the general believers who may be swayed by temptation and the infallible Imams who are protected from Satan’s influence. It reinforces the idea that spiritual bondage is a result of choice rather than predestination, aligning with the broader Quranic narrative of the test of humanity.
